O3_reason_to_dismiss: Stored internal formulas are server-generated, so once typing rejects a user 4th argument a solver can argue already-persisted 4-arg internal formulas and the JSONBArrayGetElement class itself need no change (and must keep working for legacy rows).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legacy internal formulas carrying a legitimate 4th template must keep evaluating, including date_with_time rows whose stored mode is 'date' but whose template casts to timestamptz; first()/last() delegate to index() and must keep working; per-type templates (single_file '{elem}', select '-> value', numeric/boolean/interval casts) must stay distinct. Forcing every 4-arg form to the text default or rejecting stored 4-arg formulas breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a slice/at-style shortcut that forwards an extra user literal (e.g. a cast or path) into a template-based JSONB expression
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: first()/last() already delegate to index() with extra args; a maintainer adding a generalised accessor would reuse the same literal-carrying pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: JSONBSingleInnerKeyArrayExpression formats key/type strings straight into SQL; a variant taking inner_key_name from a formula literal would be the same mechanism
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already str.format()s inner_key_name and data types into the SQL text; only the callers keep them constant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: JSONBArrayJoinValues-style expression with a user-chosen JSON key spliced into the template instead of compiled as a parameter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Neighbouring JSONB helpers mix fixed SQL templates and compiled params; making the 'value' key configurable is a natural feature request.
